correctness.rationale: For both explicitly specified sixteen-vertex diameter-two graphs, a set is geodesic general-position exactly when it avoids induced three-vertex paths. Direct computation exhaustively enumerates 65,536 subsets each, tests a second component-clique membership condition, and obtains the displayed full face vectors. Two independent exact mod-two row and column rank reductions of all augmented boundary maps agree, as do boundary-composition and Euler checks, giving exactly 57 degree-three classes for Shrikhande and 98 degree-three plus one degree-four class for rook.

value.rationale: The two canonical nonisomorphic graphs with the same strongly regular parameters (16,6,2,2) have distinct complete mod-two geodesic general-position topology, including a degree-four class only for the rook complex. This is a natural metric-combinatorial discriminator with motivated exact finite domain and demonstrates that adjacency parameters and small face counts alone fail to determine topology. No generic or paper-sized extension is needed for this exact natural invariant.
